Pixel Space End-to-End Learning Hierarchy

The same particles form three isolated modules. The middle module becomes the hand from the source GIF. The hand starts at finger contact and plays the snap. The hand, encoder, and decoder then change together into one connected particle flow and form HiT.

Better image quality.
Less FLOPs.

HiT reaches the same image quality with fewer training FLOPs.

HiT learns its own
visual hierarchy.

HiT organizes patches at test time and generates images directly in pixel space.

Test-time image grouping

HiT forms compact groups for each image and diffusion timestep. Both group membership and group counts adapt to the input.

Groups can follow object parts, combine background regions, and connect distant patches.

The router learns during training. It forms the groups during both training and generation.

No segmentation labels. No pretrained visual encoder.

One more thing.

Images and words.
One hierarchy.

HiT connects image regions and caption words through a shared hierarchy.

These connections emerge without word–region annotations.
